editorial:
Imagine spending your whole life believing in crazy secrets, only to find out that one of them is actually real. You'll meet Jerry, a guy who spends his days writing letters to anyone who will listen about government cover-ups. He is mostly ignored until he meets Alice, a taxi driver who thinks he is just a bit nuts. The vibe is a cool mix of a romantic comedy and a scary spy movie. It starts off feeling light and funny, but it quickly turns into a race for survival as mysterious men start hunting Jerry down. You get a great look at how lonely it feels to be the only person who believes the truth.

Mel Gibson is great here because he plays the role with a lot of energy, and the chemistry between the leads keeps you interested. The pacing is quick, and the mystery keeps you guessing which of his theories is the dangerous one. Some parts might feel a bit dated since it is from the 90s, but the tension still works. If you love a good mystery, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: Everything comes down to a secret about a fake death. You find out that Jerry was right about a high-ranking official who faked his death to hide his crimes. The bad guys try to kill Jerry to keep the secret safe, but Alice helps him fight back. In the end, the truth comes out, the villains are stopped, and Jerry finally gets the recognition he wanted. He and Alice end up together, proving he wasn't crazy after all.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves spy mysteries and underdog stories.
